body: Air France has received its 60th Airbus A220-300 from an order initially placed in 2019 to gradually replace its A318 and A319 fleet. On November 6, 2026, Air France said its 60th Airbus A220, registered F-HOZJ and named 'Mimizan', joined the fleet around five years after the first, registered F-HZUA and named 'Le Bourget', arrived on October 31, 2021. The carrier's latest aircraft will welcome its first customers for its first commercial flight in the coming days.

On July 30, 2019, Air France announced it had placed a firm order for 60 A220-300s, with 30 options and 30 acquisition rights to join its short- and medium-haul fleet. At the time, Benjamin Smith, CEO of the Air France-KLM Group, said that the A220-300 "demonstrates optimum environmental, operational, and economic efficiency".

In February 2026, Smith said the A220 would exclusively be used to fly the entire medium-haul mainline fleet at Air France, and he hoped to have between 90 and 95 units in place before the end of the decade. In the carrier's most recent statement in November 2026, the company said its 61st and all upcoming A220-300s will be fitted with Wi-Fi technology during their post-delivery work, and before their first commercial flight.

Air France said: "In five years, the A220 has established itself as one of the pillars of Air France's short- and medium-haul network." Operating alone or alongside Airbus A320 family aircraft, it now serves 50 destinations, from Nice to Istanbul, and from Geneva to Brest. Nearly 24 million customers have already traveled aboard it, in a spacious, bright 148-seat cabin. According to Airbus, around 720 pilots and 1,800 cabin crew members have received specific A220 training, while 300 mechanics are certified and 460 ground staff are prepared to welcome the aircraft every day. Ch-aviation data shows Air France is still actively operating three Airbus A318-100s and a single A319-100; all A318s were expected to be retired in November 2026, but Air France has extended this to March 2027.
en.summary: Air France has received its 60th Airbus A220-300, registered F-HOZJ and named 'Mimizan', completing the firm order of 60 placed in July 2019. The airline says the type now serves 50 destinations and has carried nearly 24 million passengers.
en.title: Air France receives final Airbus A220-300 from initial 2019 order

body: 法國航空已接收2019年訂單中的第60架空中巴士A220-300，逐步汰換A318與A319機隊。法航表示，第60架A220於2026年11月6日加入機隊，註冊編號F-HOZJ，命名為「米米藏」（Mimizan）；首架A220註冊編號F-HZUA，命名為「勒布爾熱」（Le Bourget），於2021年10月31日交付，相隔約5年。最新這架飛機將在未來幾天執飛首個商業航班、迎接首批旅客。
2019年7月30日，法航宣布訂購60架A220-300確定訂單，另有30架選擇權與30架購買權，用於中短程機隊。法航-荷航集團執行長班傑明·史密斯當時表示，A220-300兼具環保、營運與經濟效益，並指出該機型可大幅降低二氧化碳與噪音排放，為中短程旅客提供更舒適的客艙，也為飛行員提供配備最新導航技術的連網駕駛艙。
2026年2月，史密斯表示，A220將專門執飛法航整個中程主力機隊，並希望在2030年前機隊規模達到90至95架。法航2026年11月最新聲明指出，第61架及後續所有A220-300將在交付後作業期間、首個商業航班前加裝Wi-Fi。

法航在聲明中表示，5年來A220已成為法航中短程航網的支柱之一，單獨執飛或與空中巴士A320系列共同執飛50個目的地，從尼斯到伊斯坦堡、從日內瓦到布雷斯特，已有近2400萬名旅客搭乘，客艙為寬敞明亮的148座布局。空中巴士的資料顯示，約720名飛行員與1800名客艙組員已接受A220專門訓練，另有300名機務人員取得認證、460名地勤人員每日迎接該機型。ch-aviation資料顯示，法航現仍營運3架A318-100與1架A319-100；A318原定2026年11月全數退役，法航已延至2027年3月。
zh.summary: 法國航空已接收2019年訂單中的第60架A220-300，註冊編號F-HOZJ、命名「米米藏」，完成當年60架確定訂單；法航表示該機型現已飛航50個目的地、載運近2400萬名旅客。
